result.title: A Hierarchy of Risk Certificates for Representation-Based Prediction
result.summary: Representation-based prediction underlies many machine-learning systems. Yet a fitted predictor's failure to meet an accuracy requirement does not establish that its representation-decoder class cannot meet it. We study optimal population mean squared error (MSE) over Lipschitz decoders acting on a fixed representation. For blocks of $b\geq2$ independent and identically distributed (iid) observations, we minimize total squared error (normalized by $b-1$) under pairwise Lipschitz constraints. We prove that expected block scores form nondecreasing lower bounds on optimal class risk and converge to that risk on compact metric feature spaces, although no fixed block size provides a uniform relative guarantee. Verified dual lower bounds and iid calibration observations independent of model development, with bounded targets and predictions, yield simultaneous lower confidence bounds on optimal class risk and upper confidence bounds on fitted-predictor risk. These bounds can establish that every admissible decoder exceeds a prescribed MSE threshold or that an admissible fitted predictor meets it. Controlled experiments illustrate population-risk certification; fixed PTB-XL and Bike Sharing experiments provide deterministic empirical-risk conclusions. The results support principled assessment and selection of representation-decoder configurations. Efficient certification at scale and extensions to dependent observations remain open problems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究固定表示上 Lipschitz 解码器类的最优总体 MSE 风险，证明分块（b≥2）期望得分构成非降下界并在紧致度量特征空间上收敛，结合对偶下界与独立校准给出风险置信区间，从而判定是否存在达标解码器，并用受控实验与 PTB-XL、Bike Sharing 数据演示。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“表示-解码器类能否达标”的风险证书思路，可能可供核查 latent 内部状态是否保留足以支撑答案的视觉信息、以及信息坍缩是否已发生，但方法目前面向一般表示与 Lipschitz 解码器，向 VLM 高维视觉表示的迁移尚待验证。
